interest: For historians of interwar East Asia and U.S.–Japanese diplomacy, this file offers an invaluable real-time perspective on the critical turning point where Japan shifted from parliamentary politics toward militarism and international isolation. The pairing of detailed monthly field reports from the Tokyo Embassy with internal State Department Far Eastern Affairs analytical memoranda allows researchers to observe not only events on the ground—such as Diet debates, press censorship, right-wing terrorist plots, and military defiance—but also how Washington interpreted and synthesized these rapid developments. Furthermore, the file uniquely captures the inseparable nexus between external military aggression in Manchuria and domestic socioeconomic dislocation in Japan, tracing how the agrarian crisis, currency turbulence, and capital flight directly fueled ultra-nationalist radicalism and political assassinations.
overview: This file comprises monthly political reports, diplomatic despatches, and State Department Division of Far Eastern Affairs memoranda documenting Japan's internal and external affairs from July 1931 through February 1933 (with docket indexing through July 1934). Recorded primarily by the U.S. Embassy in Tokyo—notably under Ambassador Joseph C. Grew—the collection chronicles the collapse of Japanese party democracy and civilian rule amidst the acute shock of the Manchurian crisis, beginning with the Wanpaoshan affair and Mukden Incident of September 1931 through the establishment and formal recognition of Manchukuo, the Shanghai Incident, and Japan's eventual decision to withdraw from the League of Nations following the Lytton Report. Domestically, the documents trace severe financial and rural depression, the abandonment of the gold standard, soaring military budgetary demands, and the rapid ascent of military dominance accelerated by ultra-nationalist violence, including the Blood Brotherhood assassinations, the May 15, 1932 assassination of Prime Minister Tsuyoshi Inukai, and the subsequent establishment of Admiral Viscount Makoto Saito's national coalition cabinet.
